figures.caption: Table 1. Main comparison (Gemma-MoE; full test splits). Energy MAE, pMAE, and severe-error rate (sev); portion MAE and pMAE. Bold = best, underline = second best per dataset; ↓ lower is better.

Table 7. Per-backbone results: direct vs. grounded agent (energy/portion MAE; sev = % of meals off by >100 kcal; full splits). Bold = agent better than direct. Energy here is the raw decompose-and-sum; the deployed system routes energy by cuisine (Table 9) and takes portion from the agent.
Figure 1. Open-KNEAD overview. Input is a single meal image, processed locally; the output is assembled by routing each quantity to the path that estimates it best.

Figure 3. Portion MAE, direct vs. Open-KNEAD agent, across every backbone × dataset. Each backbone is a direct estimate (dot) connected to the agent estimate. Dotted lines mark frontier closed-model direct estimates (gpt-5.5, Gemini).

Figure 2. Qualitative trace. One OmniFood meal end to end (Gemma-MoE): the agent grounds each item to an FNDDS code and food name and recovers the invisible cooking oil, lifting energy from 378 to 706 against a 727 kcal ground truth.
Table 13. Vision mechanisms that did not improve estimation (single-image, local-inference scope). Each was probed and treated as a boundary, not adopted.

Table 12. Meal-level macronutrient estimation (Gemma-MoE; full test splits). MAE and pMAE for protein, fat, and carbohydrate. Bold = best, underline = second best per dataset (lower better). Macronutrients are routed together with energy (Path A, or Path B+recipe by cuisine), so Open-KNEAD tracks the direct estimate except where the recipe-prior applies, most visibly OmniFood fat (oil).

Figure 4. Grounding lowers per-item portion error. Per-item portion MAE, ungrounded structured (x) vs. grounded agent (y), one point per backbone × dataset; points below y = x favor grounding (12 of 15).
Table 10. Per-ingredient MAE, all backbones: grounded agent vs. ungrounded structured (GT-matched items). Bold = grounded lower.

Table 5. The food-dataset landscape (full). Evaluating agentic nutrition estimation needs real plated meals with measured nutrients, mass, and per-ingredient ground truth; only the three we adopt (bottom) provide all three. (∼ = partial.)
